title: Beyond Benchmarks: Disagreement Among Frontier LLMs on Real-World Fact-Checks
byline: Jordanov, Kosta, Yordanov, David, Jordanova, Yana
excerpt:
Abstract

Frontier large language models achieve comparable accuracy on public benchmarks, a parity often read as evidence that they are interchangeable as assessors of factual claims. We test that assumption directly, on claims not drawn from any public benchmark. Five frontier models were each asked to adjudicate 1,000 real-world claims submitted by users to a fact-checking platform. They were tasked with assigning every claim a verdict on a five-point scale from True to False, as well as reporting their confidence in each answer.

On the 997 claims where all five models returned a usable verdict, they fail to reach consensus on 63%, and on 23% the two furthest-apart verdicts differ by at least two verdict categories. The ordinal Krippendorff’s α of 0.77 reflects structured but far from interchangeable judgement. We find that disagreement concentrates in the intermediate verdicts, where claims resist clean adjudication: the definitive poles are unanimous about half the time, against roughly one in ten for the intermediate verdicts.

In relation to disagreement, our results show that model confidence is not a reliable indicator of whether the panel will agree. The models are highly confident almost everywhere, rating 76% of answers 9 or 10 on a 1–10 confidence scale, yet they agree with one another on confidence markedly less than on the verdicts themselves (α = 0.44). The verdict that is given to an assertion will then depend heavily on which model one consults, which matters a great deal as more people turn to such models to verify information.

Key findings:

  • On 63% of claims (632 / 997; 95% CI 60–66%) at least one model dissents from the panel majority, or no majority forms at all.
  • On 23% of claims (232 / 997; 95% CI 21–26%), the two furthest-apart verdicts differ by at least two verdict categories — an actual dispute over the claim, not a difference in calibration.
  • The ordinal Krippendorff's α of 0.77, across 5 models on 997 claims, reflects structured but far from interchangeable judgement.
  • Disagreement concentrates in the intermediate verdicts, where claims resist clean adjudication: the definitive poles are unanimous about half the time, against roughly one in ten for the intermediate verdicts.
  • The models are highly confident almost everywhere, rating 76% of answers 9 or 10 on a 1–10 confidence scale, yet they agree with one another on confidence markedly less than on the verdicts themselves (α = 0.44).

描述

抽象的

前沿大型语言模型在公共基准上达到了相当的准确性，这种同等性通常被解读为它们作为事实主张的评估者可以互换的证据。 我们根据并非来自任何公共基准的声明直接测试该假设。 五个前沿模型分别被要求裁决用户向事实核查平台提交的 1,000 条真实世界的主张。 他们的任务是按照从真到假的五分制对每个说法进行判定，并报告他们对每个答案的信心。

在 997 个索赔中，所有五个模型都返回了可用的判决，其中 63% 的人未能达成共识，而在 23% 的情况下，两个相距最远的判决至少有两个判决类别不同。 序数 Krippendorff 的 α 为 0.77，反映了结构化但远非可互换的判断。 我们发现分歧集中在中间裁决中，其中的主张抵制干净的裁决：最终的极点大约有一半的时间是一致的，而中间裁决的比例大约为十分之一。

关于分歧，我们的结果表明模型置信度并不是专家组是否同意的可靠指标。 这些模型几乎在所有地方都具有很高的置信度，在 1-10 置信度范围内将 76% 的答案评为 9 或 10，但它们在置信度上的一致性明显低于结论本身 (α = 0.44)。 对断言的判决将在很大程度上取决于所参考的模型，随着越来越多的人转向此类模型来验证信息，这一点非常重要。

主要发现：

  • 在 63% 的索赔中（632 / 997；95% CI 60-66%），至少有一种模型与专家组多数意见不同，或者根本没有形成多数意见。
  • 对于 23% 的索赔（232 / 997；95% CI 21-26%），两个相距最远的判决至少有两个判决类别不同——对索赔的实际争议，而不是校准上的差异。
  • 在 997 项索赔的 5 个模型中，序数 Krippendorff 的 α 值为 0.77，反映了结构化但远非可互换的判断。
  • 分歧集中在中间判决上，其中的主张抵制干净的裁决：最终的两极大约有一半的时间是一致的，而中间判决的比例约为十分之一。
  • 这些模型几乎在所有地方都具有很高的置信度，在 1-10 置信度范围内将 76% 的答案评为 9 或 10，但它们在置信度上的一致性明显低于结论本身 (α = 0.44)。
